trigger: A session with auth_source engine_token and stored principal_kind human; reachable only through a hand-edited durable sessions row (sessions has no CHECK on those columns, session_store.cpp:136-150) because AuthRoutes::synthesize_token_session (auth_routes.cpp:401-415) sets both fields and token sessions are not persisted.
summary: Decision sites (auth_routes.cpp require_permission/require_scoped_permission/require_list_read, authz_gates.cpp) and audit class stamps (auth_routes.cpp, mcp_server.cpp) compare the stored principal_kind alone while Session::is_engine() is the canonical engine discriminator.
classification_rationale: Pre-existing and untouched by this range. Facts: I1 and I3 if the split state were reached. E6 is applied (wrong outcome cannot occur in production): the only creator of an engine_token session, AuthRoutes::synthesize_token_session (auth_routes.cpp:401-415), sets both fields and token sessions are never persisted; every persist_new_session caller hard-codes a local, oidc or saml auth_source and sets no principal_kind, so persisted sessions are always human; the sessions table has no CHECK, so only a direct database write reaches the state, and that writer can already set role, elevated_until or forge any session, so the split gives no authority they lack. E6 rests on code reading by security-guardian, unhappy-path and chaos-injector (subagents of the authoring session, NOT independent; security-guardian itself said E6 was not fully proven because not every session-restore path was traced), so the E6 judgement is for the ADR owner to confirm and the owner is also the git author. Without E6 the derived band is HIGH. Raised independently by security-guardian (Gate 2), consistency-auditor (F1) and unhappy-path (UP-1/UP-2). Dedupe: open issue #2343 (needs-triage, not roadmap, not parked) already tracks consolidating the engine-session discriminator onto Session::is_engine(); evidence and the extended site list were added as a comment (issuecomment-6457311944). The finding carries I1, so #2343 needs a priority when triaged; it must not be parked on the roadmap. Out of scope here: the generic refusal body of get_me for a service-scoped token (enterprise-readiness NICE-1).
